newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO sees average EPS growth 7.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees average EPS growth 7.5 pct.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday it expected to achieve an average growth of earnings per share of 7.5 percent in the coming years.
"In 1997 we continue on course. Therefore, we are confident that we will achieve our average profit growth aims for the coming years," ABN AMRO's board said in its annual report.
ABN AMRO has set out a long term strategy of achieving average earnings per share growth of at least 7.5 percent.
The annual report also targeted an increase in net profits of at least 10 percent annually as a long term goal.
On February 27 ABN AMRO reported 1996 net profit rise of 26 percent to 3.30 billion guilders. Earnings per share rose to 9.26 guilders from 7.69 guilders in 1995.
The bank at the time declined to give a forecast for 1997.
ABN AMRO said it aimed for an dividend pay out ratio of between 45 and 50 percent of profits, according to its annual report.
It also aims to earn half of its profits abroad against 44 percent currently.
